userStories.title: requirePlan middleware — gate pipeline execution behind license check
userStories.description: Create Express middleware `requirePlan` that gates pipeline execution endpoints behind a valid license/plan check. The middleware reads from the `billing` table (or `workspace_env_vars` for self-hosted license key) and rejects unauthenticated plan users with a 402 response containing a structured `{ error, code: 'PLAN_REQUIRED', upgradeUrl }` payload that the frontend PaywallContext can intercept.
acceptanceCriteria: New file `backend/src/lib/require-plan.ts` exports `requirePlan` Express middleware
Middleware checks `billing` table for active subscription (`status = 'active'` OR `status = 'trialing'` within 14-day window)
Self-hosted path: checks `RORCA_LICENSE_KEY` env var; if set and valid RS256 JWT, allow request
Returns HTTP 402 with `{ error: 'Plan required', code: 'PLAN_REQUIRED', upgradeUrl: 'https://rorca.app/pricing' }` when check fails
Middleware is applied to `POST /api/pipeline/trigger` and `POST /api/pipeline/retry` routes only
All other routes remain ungated (spec generation, direction, memory, workspaces remain free)
Unit test: returns 402 when no billing row exists
Unit test: returns next() when billing.status = 'active'
Unit test: returns next() when valid RORCA_LICENSE_KEY env var is present
TypeScript: no type errors, `requirePlan` is typed as `RequestHandler`

userStories.title: 14-day Pro trial — auto-provision trial on first workspace registration
userStories.description: When a user registers their first workspace, automatically provision a 14-day Pro trial row in the `billing` table. The trial row has `status = 'trialing'`, `trial_ends_at = NOW() + INTERVAL '14 days'`, `plan = 'pro'`, `workspace_id = NULL` (workspace-agnostic). No credit card required. Trial expiry is checked by `requirePlan` middleware.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration `20260316000002_billing_trial_columns.sql` adds `trial_ends_at TIMESTAMPTZ` and `trial_started_at TIMESTAMPTZ` columns to `billing` table if not present

`POST /api/workspaces` route: after inserting first workspace, inserts a `billing` row with `status='trialing'`, `plan='pro'`, `trial_started_at=NOW()`, `trial_ends_at=NOW()+14days` if no billing row exists yet
`requirePlan` middleware (BL-001) treats `status='trialing'` AND `trial_ends_at > NOW()` as valid
Once `trial_ends_at < NOW()` the trial is expired — `requirePlan` rejects with 402
`GET /api/billing` response includes `{ trialEndsAt, daysRemaining, isTrialing }` fields
Unit test: first workspace registration creates billing trial row
Unit test: second workspace registration does NOT create duplicate billing row
Unit test: expired trial (trial_ends_at in past) causes requirePlan to return 402

userStories.title: RSA key pair generation — RORCA_LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY for offline license signing
userStories.description: Add a setup utility that generates an RS256 RSA key pair for offline license signing. The private key is stored as `RORCA_LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY` env var (for cloud/self-hosted to sign licenses). The public key is bundled into the backend binary for offline verification. Add a CLI command `rorca generate-license-key` that outputs a fresh RS256 key pair.
acceptanceCriteria: New file `backend/src/lib/license-crypto.ts` exports `generateKeyPair()`, `signLicense(payload, privateKey)`, `verifyLicense(token, publicKey)` functions
`generateKeyPair()` uses Node `crypto.generateKeyPairSync('rsa', { modulusLength: 2048 })` and returns `{ privateKey, publicKey }` as PEM strings
`signLicense(payload, privateKey)` signs a JWT with RS256 algorithm, expiry 1 year, issuer 'rorca.app'
`verifyLicense(token, publicKey)` verifies the JWT and returns `{ valid, payload }` — never throws, returns `{ valid: false }` on error
Bundled public key stored at `backend/src/lib/license-public-key.pem` (placeholder — actual key generated at build time)
`RORCA_LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY` env var used by `signLicense` if set; falls back to error if not set
New script `backend/scripts/generate-license-key.ts` prints a fresh RS256 key pair when run with `npx tsx`
Unit tests: sign + verify roundtrip succeeds; tampered token returns `{ valid: false }; expired token returns `{ valid: false }`

userStories.title: License activation endpoint — POST /api/billing/activate-license
userStories.description: Add `POST /api/billing/activate-license` endpoint that accepts a license key JWT, verifies it with the bundled RS256 public key, and if valid upserts the `billing` table row to `status='active'`, `plan=payload.plan`, `license_key=token`, `activated_at=NOW()`. Used by both cloud-issued licenses and self-hosted offline activation.
acceptanceCriteria: `POST /api/billing/activate-license` accepts `{ licenseKey: string }` body
Verifies JWT with `verifyLicense()` from BL-003; rejects with 422 `{ error: 'Invalid license key' }` if invalid
Upserts `billing` row: `status='active'`, `plan=payload.plan`, `license_key=licenseKey`, `activated_at=NOW()`, `expires_at=payload.exp` (if present)
Returns `{ activated: true, plan, expiresAt }` on success
Idempotent: activating the same key twice returns success (upsert, not insert)
New migration `20260316000004_billing_license_columns.sql` adds `license_key TEXT`, `activated_at TIMESTAMPTZ`, `expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ` columns to billing table
`GET /api/billing` response updated to include `licenseKey` (last 8 chars only), `activatedAt`, `expiresAt`
Unit test: valid license key activates successfully
Unit test: invalid/tampered license key returns 422
Unit test: GET /api/billing shows license info after activation

`PaywallModal` component: centered overlay, semi-transparent backdrop, shows plan name ('Rorca Pro'), 3 key features list, 'Start Free Trial' and 'Activate License' CTAs, 'Learn More' link

'Start Free Trial' CTA navigates to `window.location.href = upgradeUrl` (Stripe checkout URL from 402 payload)
'Activate License' CTA opens an inline form to paste a license key (calls BL-004 endpoint)
`PaywallProvider` wraps `<App>` in `src/main.tsx`

userStories.title: Stripe checkout flow — POST /api/billing/create-checkout-session
userStories.description: Add Stripe checkout integration. `POST /api/billing/create-checkout-session` creates a Stripe Checkout Session for the Pro plan and returns the checkout URL. `POST /api/billing/webhook` handles Stripe webhook events (checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated, customer.subscription.deleted) to update the billing table.
acceptanceCriteria: New file `backend/src/lib/stripe-client.ts` initializes Stripe SDK with `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` env var; exports `stripe` instance

`POST /api/billing/create-checkout-session` creates Stripe Checkout Session with: mode='subscription', price ID from `STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID` env var, success_url and cancel_url pointing back to frontend
Returns `{ checkoutUrl }` — frontend redirects user to Stripe-hosted checkout
`POST /api/billing/webhook` endpoint: verifies `Stripe-Signature` header using `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, parses event
On `checkout.session.completed`: upserts `billing` row with `status='active'`, `stripe_customer_id`, `stripe_subscription_id`, `plan='pro'`
On `customer.subscription.updated`: updates `billing.status` to `active` or `past_due` based on subscription status
On `customer.subscription.deleted`: updates `billing.status='canceled'`
Migration `20260316000007_billing_stripe_columns.sql` adds `stripe_customer_id TEXT`, `stripe_subscription_id TEXT` columns
Stripe webhook endpoint uses raw body parser (not json) for signature verification
Unit test: webhook handler upserts billing row on checkout.session.completed
Unit test: invalid webhook signature returns 400

userStories.title: Trial expiry notification and grace period
userStories.description: Send in-app notifications as trial nears expiry. At 7 days, 3 days, 1 day, and 0 days remaining, create a notification in the `notification_history` table. The NotificationContext in the frontend displays these. Add a 3-day grace period after trial expiry — `requirePlan` allows requests during grace but sets `X-Grace-Period: true` response header.
acceptanceCriteria: New cron job in `backend/src/lib/scheduler.ts` runs daily: queries billing rows where `status='trialing'` and checks days remaining
At 7, 3, 1 days remaining: inserts into `notification_history` with `type='trial_expiring'`, `title='Trial expires in N days'`, `body` with upgrade CTA
At 0 days (expired): inserts `type='trial_expired'` notification
Notifications are idempotent — checks if notification for that day already exists before inserting (dedup by `type + DATE(created_at)`)
`requirePlan` middleware: if `trial_ends_at` is between 0 and 3 days ago, allow request but set `X-Rorca-Grace-Period: true` response header
After 3-day grace period, `requirePlan` returns 402 normally
Frontend `NotificationContext` shows trial expiry notifications in the notification bell
Unit test: daily cron creates notification at 7-day mark

userStories.title: Plan enforcement guard for active pipeline runs
userStories.description: Ensure that plan expiry mid-run does not abort active pipeline runs. The `requirePlan` check only fires at trigger time — already-running pipelines complete regardless of plan state. Add a `plan_checked_at` field to `pipeline_runs` so audit logs capture the plan state at trigger time.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration `20260316000011_pipeline_runs_plan_checked_at.sql` adds `plan_checked_at TIMESTAMPTZ` and `plan_at_trigger TEXT` columns to `pipeline_runs`
`POST /api/pipeline/trigger` sets `plan_checked_at = NOW()` and `plan_at_trigger = billing.plan` when inserting the pipeline run
`requirePlan` middleware is NOT applied to in-flight run management endpoints (`GET /api/pipeline/runs`, `POST /api/pipeline/cancel`, `POST /api/pipeline/retry`)
Only `POST /api/pipeline/trigger` is gated — once a run is queued it proceeds to completion
Worker process does NOT re-check plan before executing each story — only trigger-time check matters
Audit log: `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id` response includes `planCheckedAt` and `planAtTrigger`
Unit test: pipeline run inserted with plan_checked_at set

userStories.title: Billing webhook idempotency — prevent duplicate billing state transitions
userStories.description: Stripe can deliver webhooks multiple times. Add idempotency handling to `POST /api/billing/webhook` using the Stripe event ID. Store processed event IDs in a `stripe_webhook_events` table. If the same event ID arrives again, return 200 without processing.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration `20260316000012_stripe_webhook_events.sql` creates table `stripe_webhook_events (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, event_type TEXT NOT NULL, processed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW())`
`POST /api/billing/webhook` handler: before processing, checks if `stripe_webhook_events` contains the event ID
If found: returns 200 immediately (idempotent success)
If not found: processes event, then inserts into `stripe_webhook_events` within the same transaction
Old events cleaned up by a weekly cron (delete rows older than 90 days)
Unit test: duplicate event ID returns 200 without updating billing table
Unit test: new event ID processes and inserts idempotency record

userStories.title: Self-hosted offline license activation — RORCA_LICENSE_KEY env var
userStories.description: Self-hosted instances (users running `rorca start` locally) can activate with an offline RS256 license JWT via the `RORCA_LICENSE_KEY` environment variable. New admin endpoint `POST /api/admin/generate-license` (requires `RORCA_ADMIN_KEY` header): accepts `{ plan, email, expiresInDays }`, signs with `RORCA_LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY`, returns license JWT

Backend startup log prints: 'License: self-hosted (RORCA_LICENSE_KEY)' or 'License: trial (N days remaining)' or 'License: not configured'

userStories.title: GitHub OAuth minimal scope strategy — request only read:user + user:email
userStories.description: The GitHub OAuth flow currently requests broad scopes. Update to request only `read:user` and `user:email` for initial sign-in. Repo access (`repo` scope) should only be requested at the point where the user actually connects a workspace to GitHub (lazy scope elevation). This matches GitHub's recommended minimal scope strategy and improves OAuth consent UX.
acceptanceCriteria: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts` GitHub OAuth callback: initial scope is `read:user user:email` only

GitHub connection for workspace (Settings > GitHub Integration): triggers a second OAuth flow requesting `repo` scope with a clear explanation: 'Rorca needs repo access to create PRs and read commits for this workspace'
The second OAuth flow uses GitHub's incremental authorization — the user already has a session token with read:user, the new flow only asks for the additional `repo` scope
Token storage: `github_connections` table stores `scope TEXT` column showing which scopes were granted
Migration `20260316000014_github_connections_scope.sql` adds `scope TEXT DEFAULT 'read:user user:email'` to `github_connections`
UI: Settings > GitHub shows scope badge next to connection (e.g., 'read:user' or 'full repo access')
'Upgrade access' button visible when connection has only `read:user` scope — triggers incremental OAuth
Unit test: initial OAuth callback stores read:user scope
Unit test: workspace GitHub connection flow requests repo scope
